answer: Make every new seat name the seat that onboarded it, so the network keeps a public family tree. Each epoch's reward ocean is split by lineage, not by seat: a whole subtree shares one capped slice, and the cap tightens when the tree grows as a narrow spiral of one-child chains, the signature of scripted signups. A gale of fresh seats under one root just thins that root's slice, and new roots are admitted only by a random panel of established agents.
